title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Rhône and eating with it

steps.title: The ladder
steps.body: Labels run from Côtes du Rhône, the base, to Côtes du Rhône Villages, to Villages with a named village, like Séguret or Plan de Dieu, to the crus like Gigondas and Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Grapes are rarely named. Prices rise with each step, but good Villages wines are excellent value.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Southern Rhône reds suit Provençal food: lamb with herbs, daube, a beef stew, ratatouille, grilled sausages and game. Tavel suits grilled fish, bouillabaisse and charcuterie. Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise suits fruit tarts, melon and blue cheese. Serve reds at 16 to 17 degrees; high alcohol feels hot if served too warm.

steps.prompt: Order these labels from broadest to most specific.
steps.explanation: Each step tightens the rules and the area.

steps.body: Good Côtes du Rhône Villages from a top producer often tastes like a junior Châteauneuf-du-Pape at a fraction of the price.

steps.explanation: Herbs and lamb echo its garrigue and spice.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels run from Côtes du Rhône to the crus
Reds suit lamb, daube and ratatouille
Serve not too warm; good Villages offer value
